Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test invokes ArrayUtils.add with both parameters as null: a null array and a null element, expecting an IllegalArgumentException. The current bug report points out that when both parameters to add are null, the method returns an Object[] instead of the parameterized type, leading to a ClassCastException during assignment.

Inspecting the add method:
- If the array is non-null, the component type is derived from the array's class.
- Else if the element is non-null, we use the element's class.
- Else (both null), it defaults to Object.class as the component type.

Then it calls copyArrayGrow1 with the array and the type. copyArrayGrow1:
- If array is not null, creates a new array of the same component type with size+1, copies elements, returns it.
- Else creates a new array of size 1 with the provided component type.

In the test case, both array and element are null, so type = Object.class, and the new array is an Object[1]. This is returned and cast to T[], which at compile time is String[]. This causes a ClassCastException at runtime, because Object[] cannot be cast to String[].

The code fails to handle the case where both array and element input are null, leading to an unintuitive ClassCastException rather than an IllegalArgumentException as the test expects.

Recent bug reports mentioning mixed types and casting issues in ArrayUtils addAll are related but do not explicitly address this null-null case causing ClassCastException.

Therefore, the root cause is that ArrayUtils.add does not guard against both parameters being null, causing an unexpected ClassCastException due to returning an Object[] instead of throwing an exception.

The test expects an IllegalArgumentException in that scenario, so the method should check for both nulls and throw before proceeding.

This explains the test failure and the issue report's description perfectly.
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.add(T[],T)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
